stories.headline: Two tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Trump weighs new Iran strikes; Brent tops $92

key_facts.fact: Two crude oil tankers — one Saudi-flagged and one South Korean-owned — were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening, Aug. 31, according to Greece-based maritime risk group Marisks.
key_facts.excerpt: Two crude oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening, Greece-based maritime risk organization Marisks said on Tuesday. A South Korean-owned vessel was hit just minutes after a Saudi-flagged tanker, both on their way out of the Persian Gulf via southern shipping lanes touted as open and safe by the Trump administration.

key_facts.fact: Oil rose about 2% on Tuesday for a second straight day, with Brent above $92 a barrel and US crude at $88, after the weekend flare-up and Trump's threat to hit Iran 'hard'.
key_facts.excerpt: Both main crude contracts were up more than 2%, extending the previous day's similar jump. International benchmark Brent crude was trading early Tuesday over $92 a barrel, while U.S. crude was selling for $88.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Aug. 31 he might order further strikes, calling the six-month conflict 'a relatively little war for us' and describing Iran as 'a failed nation'.
key_facts.excerpt: "This is a relatively little war for us. This is not a big war," the president said. "They're a failed nation," Mr. Trump said of Iran. He later added, "That doesn't mean we won't smack them. We'll see what happens."

key_facts.fact: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said late Monday that a tanker leaving the strait reported being hit by three 'unknown projectiles' just off the northeastern edge of Oman, with no known casualties or environmental impact.
key_facts.excerpt: A tanker leaving the strait reported being hit by three "unknown projectiles" just off the northeastern edge of Oman, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said late Monday, noting that there were no known environmental impacts or casualties.

key_facts.fact: Iranian state media reported three people killed in the US strike on Larak Island; Trump said all missiles fired at US forces were shot down except one deemed non-threatening, and Jordan's army said it intercepted eight missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: State media reported that three people were killed in the US attack Sunday on Larak, with several others wounded. ... But Trump told Fox that all the missiles fired at US forces had been shot down, except for one that was determined not to pose a threat. Jordan's army said it had intercepted eight missiles, without stating their origin.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking at the G20 finance meeting in Asheville, said Washington will keep tightening economic pressure and that a turning point could come 'within weeks or months'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are going to continue exerting pressure, and we've had very good discussions here already," Bessent told reporters at a G20 meeting in North Carolina. He said a turning point in the pressure campaign could come "within weeks or months".

key_facts.fact: US Central Command dismissed Iran's claim that a supertanker struck sea mines in the strait as 'yet another IRGC attempt to intimidate regional commercial shipping through disinformation'.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military's Central Command dismissed on Monday a claim by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to have struck a supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz with sea mines, calling it "yet another IRGC attempt to intimidate regional commercial shipping through disinformation."

stories.headline: Israel signs €3B 'Achilles Shield' deal to build Greece's layered air defense network

key_facts.fact: Israel and Greece signed a €3 billion (about $3.5 billion) government-to-government deal on Monday, Aug. 31, under which Israel will build Greece a multi-layered air defense system called Achilles Shield.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel and Greece signed a €3 billion ($3.5 billion) defense deal on Monday under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defense system for Greece as Athens pushes ahead with a broader military modernization program.

key_facts.fact: The package covers Rafael's David's Sling and SPYDER systems, Israel Aerospace Industries' BARAK MX, ELTA multi-mission radars, and a new national command-and-control system developed by Rafael.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the deal, Israel will supply Greece with the David's Sling and SPYDER systems produced by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and the BARAK MX system made by Israel Aerospace Industries, as well as MMR multi-mission radars for air surveillance, manufactured by IAI unit ELTA Systems. ... Under Monday's deal, Greece will also receive a new national command-and-control system, developed by Rafael.

key_facts.fact: Israel's Defense Ministry called it the largest defense export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations and one of the largest in Israel's history; it was signed in Tel Aviv by ministry director general Amir Baram and his Greek counterpart Ioannis Bouras.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry said it is the "largest defense export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations, and one of the largest in the history of the State of Israel." The deal was signed on Monday at the ministry headquarters in Tel Aviv by Defense Ministry Director General Amir Baram and his Greek counterpart, Ioannis Bouras.

key_facts.fact: A supplementary €26 million agreement covers Rafael's Drone Dome systems to protect strategic sites against drones.
key_facts.excerpt: The statement said that a supplementary deal, valued at €26 million, was also signed today for the sale of Rafael's Drone Dome systems.

key_facts.fact: Athens plans to spend about €28 billion by 2036 on the Achilles Shield program plus up to 40 F-35 fighter jets from the US and frigates from France and Italy.
key_facts.excerpt: Athens plans to spend about €28 billion by 2036 to build the Achilles Shield multi-layer anti-ballistic, anti-aircraft and anti-drone system, and to buy up to 40 F-35 fighter jets from the U.S. and frigates from France and Italy.

key_facts.fact: The deal, negotiated over three years, makes Greece the second EU member to buy David's Sling after Finland; Israeli weapons exports hit a record of more than $19 billion last year, up 30% from 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel said the agreement, negotiated over three years, is one of the largest in the country's history. ... Israeli weapons exports reached record highs with more than $19bn last year, a 30 percent increase from 2024, according to official data. ... Greece is the second European Union member to agree to buy the David's Sling system, after Finland.

key_facts.fact: The alliance is rooted in shared concerns about regional rival and fellow NATO member Turkey, amid long-standing eastern Mediterranean sea-boundary disputes.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel signed a multibillion-dollar deal Monday to build an air defense shield in Greece, strengthening an alliance between the Mediterranean countries rooted in shared concerns about regional rival Turkey.

stories.headline: Himalayan flood toll tops 1,000 across Nepal and Tibet as mass burials begin

key_facts.fact: The combined death toll from last week's Nepal-China flash floods passed 1,000 as of Tuesday, Sept. 1, with more than 4,400 people still unaccounted for.
key_facts.excerpt: Death toll: The number of people killed following last week's Nepal-China flash floods topped 1,000. More than 4,400 people remained unaccounted for in both countries, officials say.

key_facts.fact: Nepal's disaster agency counted 987 deaths and 3,916 missing, including 583 foreigners; Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing in Tibet, including 261 foreigners.
key_facts.excerpt: Nepal's disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners.

key_facts.fact: Nepal began mass burials on Monday, Aug. 31, burying hundreds of unidentified bodies because it lacked freezing facilities and remains were decomposing in humid weather.
key_facts.excerpt: Nepal on Monday began mass burials for the hundreds of people killed in catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border last week... Overwhelmed by the number of bodies and without proper freezing facilities, Nepali authorities have had to begin burials before completing the identification process.

key_facts.fact: Rescue teams aided by Chinese and Indian experts are trying to reach 933 hydropower workers believed trapped inside blocked project tunnels at 11 hydropower projects.
key_facts.excerpt: 933 workers missing from 11 hydropower projects in flood-hit region ... Nepal's rescue teams, helped by Chinese and Indian experts, stepped up efforts on Monday to reach hundreds of people believed to be stuck inside blocked hydropower project tunnels in the aftermath of last week's Himalayan flood.

key_facts.fact: Nepal has deployed 20,819 security personnel and rescued 10,451 people, including 252 foreign nationals, with 411 helicopter flights so far.
key_facts.excerpt: Search, rescue, and relief operations have intensified, with 20,819 security personnel deployed across the affected districts. ... Authorities reported that 10,451 people have been rescued to date. Aerial operations have played a central role, with 411 helicopter flights conducted so far.

key_facts.fact: Satellite analysis indicates bedrock beneath a Himalayan glacier collapsed, a rockfall so extreme it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event; China has linked the disaster to climate change.
key_facts.excerpt: Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayas had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

key_facts.fact: The UN says it is Nepal's deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake, with 65,000 people needing emergency water, sanitation and hygiene support.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent flash flooding is now Nepal's deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake ... 65,000 people require emergency water, sanitation and hygiene.

stories.headline: Aon to buy insurance broker USI from KKR for $17B, its biggest deal ever

key_facts.fact: Aon announced on Aug. 31 a definitive agreement to acquire USI Insurance Services from KKR and other shareholders for a total purchase price of $17.0 billion, all cash.
key_facts.excerpt: DUBLIN, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aon plc (NYSE: AON), a leading global professional services firm, today announced the signing of a definitive agreement to acquire USI from KKR and other shareholders for a total purchase price of $17.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: The net price of $16.7 billion, after about $278 million of tax attributes, represents roughly 14.5x synergized trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA.
key_facts.excerpt: The purchase price for USI is $17.0 billion, or $16.7 billion on a net basis, which reflects approximately $278 million of certain tax attributes. The net purchase price represents approximately 14.5x on a synergized trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA basis.

key_facts.fact: USI has $3.0 billion in revenue and $1.2 billion in synergized adjusted EBITDA; Aon targets $395 million in annual run-rate net EBITDA synergies and says the deal is dilutive to adjusted EPS in 2027 and accretive from 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue: $3.0B • Synergized Adjusted EBITDA: $1.2B • Net purchase price multiple of 14.5x synergized Adjusted EBITDA • Adjusted EPS impact: dilutive in 2027, accretive in 2028 and thereafter • Net Adjusted EBITDA synergies: $395MM

key_facts.fact: The deal is being funded entirely with new debt across a range of maturities; Aon expects to keep its Baa2/A- ratings and deleverage to a 2.8-3.0x objective within about 24 months of close.
key_facts.excerpt: All cash consideration, to be funded with debt raised across a range of maturities, subject to market conditions • We [expect] to maintain our current credit ratings of Baa2 with Moody's and A- with S&P and delever to our 2.8-3.0x objective in approximately 24 months of close

key_facts.fact: For KKR, the implied equity value represents about a 6.0x return on the equity it invested in USI in 2017 and is expected to generate roughly $2.0 billion of after-tax net income for the firm.
key_facts.excerpt: The implied equity value represents an approximately 6.0x return on the equity KKR invested in 2017, and a 3.4x return on the total KKR balance sheet capital invested over the life of KKR's investment in USI. ... the transaction is expected to generate approximately $2.0 billion of ANI for KKR or $2.00 per share of ANI.

key_facts.fact: USI chairman and CEO Mike Sicard will become president of Aon plc and global CEO of its middle-market business; closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approval.
key_facts.excerpt: USI chairman and chief executive Mike Sicard [will] become president of Aon plc and global CEO of its middle-market business, reporting directly to Aon chief executive Greg Case... Subject to regulatory sign-off, the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly to buy Merida Biosciences for up to $2.88B in autoimmune push

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly said on Monday, Aug. 31, it will acquire privately held Merida Biosciences for up to $2.875 billion in cash, covering an upfront payment plus contingent milestones that were not broken out.
key_facts.excerpt: The Indiana giant will be on the hook for up to $2.875 billion in cash, covering an upfront payment and contingent milestones. The pharma didn't provide a specific financial breakdown in its news release on Monday morning.

key_facts.fact: Merida, based in Massachusetts, brings a precision degradation platform designed to selectively target and destroy pathologic antibodies driving allergic and autoimmune diseases.
key_facts.excerpt: With the acquisition of Merida Biosciences, Eli Lilly is gaining a precision degradation platform for therapies that selectively target and destroy pathologic antibodies for allergic and autoimmune diseases.

key_facts.fact: The deal strengthens Lilly's immunology portfolio with an experimental treatment for thyroid-related autoimmune conditions and is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Eli Lilly said on Monday it would acquire privately held Merida Biosciences for up to $2.88 billion in cash, strengthening its immunology portfolio with an experimental treatment for thyroid-related autoimmune conditions. ... The company expects the transaction to close in the fourth quarter.

key_facts.fact: Lilly's 2026 deal spending has outpaced prior years as it seeks to expand beyond obesity and diabetes on the back of windfall profits from its weight-loss drugs.
key_facts.excerpt: Lilly has been on an acquisition spree following windfall profits from the success of its weight-loss drugs. Its deal spending in 2026 has outpaced prior years, as the pharma giant aims to expand beyond obesity and diabetes.

stories.headline: FDA clears first new treatment for essential thrombocythemia in nearly 30 years

key_facts.fact: PharmaEssentia announced on Aug. 31 that the FDA approved BESREMi (ropeginterferon alfa-2b-njft) for adults with essential thrombocythemia, the first FDA-approved treatment for the rare blood cancer in nearly three decades.
key_facts.excerpt: PharmaEssentia USA Corporation, a subsidiary of PharmaEssentia Corporation (TWSE: 6446) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved BESREMi® (ropeginterferon alfa-2b-njft) for the treatment of adults with essential thrombocythemia (ET), making it the first new FDA-approved treatment for ET in nearly three decades.

key_facts.fact: The approval covers adults regardless of genotype or disease status, including newly diagnosed patients naive to cytoreductive therapy, and the drug is available in the US immediately.
key_facts.excerpt: BESREMi has been approved for adults with ET, regardless of their genotype or disease status, including newly diagnosed patients who are naive to cytoreductive therapy. ... BESREMi for ET is expected to be available in the United States immediately upon approval.

key_facts.fact: Approval rests on the global Phase 3 SURPASS ET trial (NCT04285086), which showed superior durable response rates and fewer thromboembolic events versus anagrelide over 12 months of treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: Supporting data for the approval came from the international phase 3 SURPASS ET trial (NCT04285086), which demonstrated durable modified European Leukemia Net (ELN) responses and hematologic control with ropeginterferon alfa. The trial showed superior durable response rates as well as reduced thromboembolic events over a year of treatment with the agent compared with anagrelide (Agrylin).

key_facts.fact: It caps a busy week for myeloproliferative neoplasms: the FDA approved Takeda and Protagonist's first-in-class rusfertide (Mimrylo) for polycythemia vera on Aug. 28, with Takeda announcing it on Aug. 31 at a list price of $4,200 per vial, or about $218,400 a year.
key_facts.excerpt: The regulatory decision announced after Friday's market close covers the treatment of erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera. Known in development as rusfertide, the once-weekly injection will reach the market under the brand name Mimrylo. ... A Takeda spokesperson said Mimrylo's list price is $4,200 per vial; assuming a single vial for each weekly dose, that price works out to $218,400 annually.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 VERIFY trial, 76.9% of patients on Mimrylo did not require therapeutic phlebotomies at 32 weeks versus 32.9% of the placebo group requiring them; Takeda has said the drug could reach $2 billion in peak revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 3 results showed 76.9% of patients treated with once-weekly injections of the study drug did not require therapeutic phlebotomies measured at 32 weeks. By comparison, 32.9% of patients in the placebo group required phlebotomies. ... Takeda has said Mimrylo could reach up to $2 billion in peak revenue.

stories.headline: Amgen's Repatha cuts risk of death 20% in patients who never had a heart attack

key_facts.fact: Amgen announced on Aug. 31 that Repatha (evolocumab) reduced the risk of dying by 20% in a study of more than 12,000 high-risk adults without a prior heart attack or stroke, when added to statins or other LDL-lowering therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: In a study of more than 12,000 high-risk patients, Repatha helped reduce the risk of dying by 20%. Treatment with Repatha led to meaningful reductions both in overall deaths and cardiovascular deaths in this pre-specified secondary analysis of VESALIUS-CV.

key_facts.fact: The results come from a pre-specified analysis of the Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV trial presented in a late-breaking science session at the European Society of Cardiology Congress 2026 in Munich and simultaneously published in Circulation.
key_facts.excerpt: The results are from a pre-specified analysis of the Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV trial and were presented in a late-breaking science session at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress 2026 in Munich, Germany. They were also simultaneously published in Circulation.

key_facts.fact: The mortality benefit began to appear after roughly 1.5 years of treatment and persisted through a median follow-up of 4.6 years; Amgen says Repatha is the first and only PCSK9 inhibitor shown to lower all-cause death risk in high-risk primary prevention patients in a Phase 3 trial.
key_facts.excerpt: The reduction in deaths began to appear after approximately 1.5 years of treatment and continued through a median follow-up of 4.6 years. ... Repatha is the First and Only PCSK9 Inhibitor Shown to Lower the Risk of Dying from All Causes, Including Cardiovascular Events, in High-Risk Primary Prevention Patients in a Phase 3 Trial

key_facts.fact: Two companion analyses showed Repatha cut first, subsequent and total cardiovascular events, and that the reduction in heart-attack risk appeared as early as six months after starting treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: One analysis showed that Repatha reduced the risk of first, subsequent and total CV events. The other analysis showed that the reduced risk of heart attack with Repatha was seen as early as six months after initiating treatment.

key_facts.fact: The headline VESALIUS-CV results, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in November 2025, had shown a 25% relative reduction in a composite of coronary heart disease death, heart attack or ischemic stroke and a 36% reduction in heart attack risk.
key_facts.excerpt: Results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in November 2025. Repatha demonstrated a 25% relative reduction in the risk of a composite of coronary heart disease (CHD) death, heart attack or ischemic stroke (3-P MACE)... Repatha also reduced the risk of heart attack by 36%.

key_facts.fact: Repatha was first approved in 2015 and has been used by roughly 9 million patients globally; it is approved in 75 countries, and the European Commission broadened its label in August 2026 based on VESALIUS-CV.
key_facts.excerpt: Repatha was first approved in 2015 and has since been used by approximately 9 million patients globally. ... In August 2026, the European Commission approved an expanded indication for the use of Repatha in adults with established or high risk for ASCVD... Repatha is approved in 75 countries.

sources.title: Amgen's Repatha Reduces Risk of Death in Patients at High Risk for a First Heart Attack or Stroke
